Currently when removing illegal content or doxing info you aren't actually removing the content. You are just moving it, where it sits in the modlog. Obviously I'm not the first person to realize this but I do have some thoughts on how to handle it.

A big issue is mod transparency, we want to keep such content actually off the site while maintaining that transparency. So my suggestion is a separate removal function, one that completely removes the content from view and sends a report to the admins as well as logs date and time the function was used in yet another mod log. This would allow moderators to actually get rid of harmful and illegal content while still being transparent and having oversight against abuse of the function, because users would be able to see the frequency of the use and admins would be able to review the actual content being removed.

Thoughts?
A better way to deal with illegal content and doxing
This is a good idea -- for now. This would work as a temporary solution, but isn't scalable if more people come to the site.
Would you mind expounding on why you believe it wont scale well?

It won't work because you're placing the burden of moderating the moderators on a small group of people. You're incorrectly assuming that moderators won't abuse this feature to remove posts they disagree with -- cluttering it such that it becomes difficult for the admins to properly arbitrate on content and focus on Voat's development. While this probably wouldn't be a problem if this idea was implemented now (said abusive admins can be blocked from using the feature, since I can't imagine there would be that many of them), it would be difficult to scale to large numbers of people.
Thanks for the explanation and insight. It was just a rough idea I had come up with so I wasn't expecting it to be implementation as is.

Actually, I don't think it would be difficult to scale. Even with expansion, unless Voat got to the size of Facebook (At that point, Voat better have other staff members anyways) moderating the mods wouldn't be such a big deal. It wouldn't be necessary until a user reports the mod for abuse anyways. The only time this would be rough is if trolls decided to report every mod they saw. With that, that person can just be banned and dealing with them would be finished.
Makes good sense. Clearly there is content that should not be able to still be viewed in the modlog, and keeping everything transparent keeps everyone honest.
